children: The spate of block deals continue on Dalal Street with shares of EPL declining as much as 9.5% on Tuesday, September 1, after a large transaction that took place in the stock.
As many as 9.15 crore shares worth ₹2,253 crore of EPL changed hands at ₹246 per share in a block deal window on Tuesday, September 1, as per the data available.

In the pre-market block deal window, 24.5 lakh shares of EPL changed hands in two block deals. The rest changed hands in a separate block. The total number of shares that have changed hands, amount to 30% of the company's outstanding equity.
The official buyers and sellers are not yet known.

On Monday, August 31, CNBC-TV18 had reported, citing sources that Blackstone-owned Epsilon Bidco Pte was set to sell up to 26.4% equity or 8.45 crore shares, in the speciality packaging company via a block deal, which could be valued at ₹1,985 crore. The offer price was said to be ₹235 apiece, the sources had added.
At the end of the June quarter promoter Epsilon Bidco Pte Ltd held 26.38% stake in EPL while public shareholding comprised 73.62%, as per data available on the stock exchanges.

Last month, EPL MD and Global CEO Hemant Bakshi told CNBC-TV18 that he has raised firm's near-term revenue growth guidance from low double digits to high teens post the June quarter where revenue grew 25%.

He said EPL successfully passed on the additional costs that came up from the West Asia crisis and was expecting to maintain the underlying earnings before interest tax depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) margin of around 20%.
Shares of EPL are trading 9.1% lower on Tuesday at ₹238.1. With this fall, the stock has trimmed its year-to-date advance down to just 10%.

title: EPL shares fall over 9% after equity worth ₹2,200 crore changes hands in block deal
